At ManoMano we moderate content at our own initiative for two reasons:

Indicator: Meaningful and comprehensible information regarding content moderation engaged in at the providers' own initiative
Value:
The platform's content moderation pipeline for out-of-scope product identification rests on a two-stage architecture: automated taxonomic classification followed by rule-based enforcement. 

In a first stage, every seller-listed product is subjected to a machine learning categorisation workflow composed of a retrieval model, which shortlists candidate leaf nodes from the platform's internal Product Information Management (PIM) taxonomy, and a supervised fine-tuned large language model (LLM) which assigns a definitive category path expressed as a hierarchical string (e.g., Plomberie > Robinetterie > Robinets). 

The PIM taxonomy tree itself encodes a scope attribute at the category root level, distinguishing IN_SCOPE from OUT_OF_SCOPE nodes; when the LLM's predicted category resolves to a node whose scope is OUT_OF_SCOPE, the product is flagged accordingly. 
Note that a complementary human review process enables the categorization into out of scope categories as well whenever business operators flag improper content into our databases.
In a second, enforcement stage, products confirmed as out-of-scope receive the platform-internal inactive reason PRODUCT_DISALLOWED, which causes immediate delisting of the corresponding offer.
